ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The CO2 fixation amounts of wheat and corn change with changes in the external CO2 concentration (as shown in the figure). May I ask: compared with C3 plants, which type of plant can C4 plants more effectively utilize low-concentration CO2?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the horizontal axis is the external CO2 concentration, labeled 100, 360, 720, 1000 mg·L^-1; the vertical axis is the CO2 fixation amount. The legend shows that the white bars represent wheat, and the gray bars represent corn. At low CO2 concentrations of 100 and 360 mg·L^-1, the CO2 fixation amounts of the gray bars (corn) are both higher than those of the white bars (wheat). Then reason: corn belongs to C4 plants, and wheat belongs to C3 plants; under low CO2 concentration, corn fixes more CO2, indicating that C4 plants can more effectively utilize low-concentration CO2.
